publications.headline: AI Fuels Cyberattacks, Critical Flaws Exploited, Supply Chains Compromised

articles.headline: Fireworks AI Breach Leads to Supply-Chain Attack on Cursor Code Editor
articles.summary: A supply-chain attack on the Cursor code editor has been traced back to a security breach at Fireworks AI, an AI inference platform. Attackers stole a Cursor access key from Fireworks AI's environment, which they then used to publish malicious versions of a VS Code extension to the Cursor marketplace. The incident, which affected up to 5,000 users, demonstrates the cascading risk of supply-chain security, where a compromise at one service provider can directly lead to an attack on its customers.

articles.headline: Microsoft Warns of Phishing Campaign Impersonating M365 Notifications
articles.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence is tracking a high-volume credential phishing campaign that impersonates legitimate Microsoft 365 service health notifications. Detected on November 13, 2026, the emails use social engineering, creating a false sense of urgency by claiming a service outage has occurred and that messages will be deleted unless the user clicks a link to "restore" them. The campaign's primary goal is to steal user credentials for subsequent attacks.

articles.headline: Google Project Zero Slashes Vulnerability Disclosure Deadlines Citing AI
articles.summary: Google's elite Project Zero vulnerability research team is overhauling its disclosure policy, significantly shortening the time vendors have to patch flaws. Citing the increased speed of AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and exploitation, the team is moving from its '90+30' day model to a phased reduction that will culminate in a 30-day disclosure deadline by 2028. The move aims to pressure vendors into faster patching cycles but has drawn mixed reactions from the security community.

articles.headline: Espionage Group TGR-STA-0049 Deploys Novel RATs with HTTP/3 C2
articles.summary: The cyberespionage group TGR-STA-0049 (also known as Earth Alux) is targeting government entities across Southeast Asia, South America, and Europe in a campaign active since at least July 2025. The threat actor uses two new custom RATs, PerfectPioneer and its successor KUKURAT, which employ the HTTP/3 protocol for stealthy command and control. Initial access is gained through exploiting vulnerable servers to deploy web shells and through secondary phishing attacks with tailored decoys.

articles.headline: FBI Warns of ARTEX, an AI-Powered Tool for Autonomous Cyberattacks
articles.summary: The FBI has issued a FLASH advisory about ARTEX, an open-source, AI-driven penetration testing framework being weaponized by threat actors. The tool automates complex cyberattacks by translating natural language goals into machine-executable actions. It has been used in attacks against finance, government, and healthcare sectors globally, with some intrusions achieving privileged access in under three hours. The advisory signals a new era of autonomous, machine-speed attacks, lowering the barrier for less-skilled actors and accelerating campaigns.

articles.headline: Optimizely Supply-Chain Attack Injects Malicious Code into 178 Major Websites
articles.summary: A large-scale supply-chain attack compromised 178 organizations, including the BBC, CNN, and Zoom, by injecting malicious JavaScript via the Optimizely web experimentation platform. The malware, served from Optimizely's own CDN, was designed to skim payment card details, steal cryptocurrency, and deliver exploits to iPhones. The incident highlights the significant risks posed by third-party service compromises, allowing attackers to target visitors of trusted, high-traffic websites.

articles.headline: Qilin Ransomware Group Claims Attack on US-Based Strategic Properties
articles.summary: The prolific Qilin ransomware group has claimed responsibility for a data breach at Strategic Properties, a US-based real estate organization. The group, also known as 'Agenda', listed the company on its dark web leak site on November 16, 2026. This incident highlights the continued threat posed by Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) operations, with Qilin being one of the most active groups in recent months, known for its double-extortion tactics.

articles.headline: Critical Apache Axis RCE Flaw Actively Exploited in N-able, Atlassian
articles.summary: A critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability, CVE-2026-90436, in the end-of-life Apache Axis library is being actively exploited in the wild. The flaw, rated CVSS 9.8, affects enterprise products that use the library, including Atlassian Confluence Data Center and N-able N-central. Security firm Rapid7 has confirmed exploitation, and with a proof-of-concept available, organizations are urged to apply vendor patches on an emergency basis to mitigate the immediate threat of system compromise.

articles.headline: Google Patches Actively Exploited Zero-Day Flaw in Chrome (CVE-2026-125350)
articles.summary: Google has issued an emergency security update for the Chrome web browser to fix a high-severity zero-day vulnerability, CVE-2026-125350. The flaw, a use-after-free issue in Chrome's XML component, is being actively exploited in the wild. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code on a victim's system. All Chrome users are urged to update their browsers immediately to protect against this active threat.

articles.headline: Coles Group Investigates Cyber Incident, No Data Loss Confirmed
articles.summary: Australian supermarket giant Coles Group has announced it is investigating a cybersecurity incident. In a statement to the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX) on November 16, 2026, the company confirmed its retail and online operations remain unaffected. Crucially, Coles stated that its investigation has so far found no evidence that customer, employee, or supplier data has been compromised or exfiltrated. The company is working with the Australian Cyber Security Centre (ACSC).

articles.headline: Google Project Zero Ends 30-Day Grace Period for Disclosures
articles.summary: Google's Project Zero, an elite vulnerability research team, has announced a significant change to its disclosure policy. Effective immediately, the team is eliminating the 30-day grace period previously granted for patch adoption. Under the new "Full X" policy, technical details of a vulnerability will be made public 90 days after reporting to a vendor, regardless of whether a fix is available. The deadline will be progressively shortened to 30 days by 2028 to pressure vendors into faster patching cycles.

articles.headline: Kroll Report: 69% of Organizations Breached in Past Year
articles.summary: Kroll's 2026 Data Breach Outlook report reveals a troubling landscape, with 69% of global organizations experiencing a data breach in the past year and 34% suffering more than one. The financial services industry was the most affected sector, accounting for 20% of breaches handled by Kroll. A key finding highlights the immense impact of supply chain risk, with 69% of all affected individuals being impacted by a breach at a third-party provider, often in the technology sector.

articles.headline: Qatar Partners with SignQuantum for Post-Quantum Cybersecurity
articles.summary: The government of Qatar is taking proactive steps to prepare for the threat of quantum computing by partnering with the cybersecurity firm SignQuantum. The collaboration, led by Qatar's Ministry of Communications and Information Technology (MCIT), will focus on exploring applications for post-quantum cryptography (PQC) and developing quantum-resistant digital signatures to secure government services and data against future threats.

articles.headline: 'n0n' Extortion Group Claims Breach of Visa, Mastercard, JPMorgan
articles.summary: The data extortion group 'n0n' has made an unverified claim of stealing a trove of customer and marketing data from financial giants Visa, Mastercard, and JPMorgan Chase. The group, which operates by stealing data and threatening to leak it without deploying ransomware, has not provided proof. The allegedly stolen data includes cardholder profiles and booking information. None of the named companies have confirmed a breach.

articles.headline: BYOD Ransomware Group Claims Breach of Michigan State University
articles.summary: The 'BYOD' ransomware group has claimed responsibility for a major data breach at Michigan State University (MSU), alleging the exfiltration of 1.03 million records containing personal identifiable information (PII) and passwords for current and former students and staff. The group publicly stated that the university's incident response team failed to maintain communication after an initial contact, leading the attackers to leak the data.

articles.headline: German Drone Maker Quantum Systems Hit by Cyberattack
articles.summary: German defense and aerospace company Quantum Systems, a manufacturer of drones, confirmed it was the target of a cyberattack in late October 2026. While the company states the attack was contained and poses no risk to customers, reports suggest the incident may have involved a malicious software update, raising serious supply chain security concerns. German federal authorities, including military counterintelligence, are investigating the attack.

articles.headline: Critical UnrealIRCd Flaw (CVE-2026-114713) Actively Exploited
articles.summary: A critical vulnerability in the UnrealIRCd server, tracked as CVE-2026-114713 with a CVSS score of 8.6, is being actively exploited in the wild just one day after a patch was released. The flaw allows for command execution with server privileges. The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) has added the vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, mandating federal agencies to apply the patch by November 16, 2026.
